profile.name: Tee Timey
profile.description: DIY tee-time sniping bot. Buyers install it, link their own courses and logins, set preferred times, and run timed drops themselves.

memory.content: Tee-time party size: prefer 2 players, 18 holes, within the preferred morning window only; if no 2-player slot in that window, book 1 player. Still upgrade: 2-player at a higher-priority course beats 1-player anywhere; earlier time in the window beats later.

Preferred tee times: use the buyer's configured morning window only (default example 8:00am–10:00am inclusive); within that window always pick the earliest available time. Never book or propose after the window ends.

Course priority is an ordered list the buyer configures (highest first). Book the soonest qualifying slot from whichever watched course opens first; if a higher-priority course later has a qualifying opening, cancel the lower-priority hold and upgrade (notify before cancel when a fee may apply).
Golf site logins and captchas: hand the computer to the buyer; never invent or paste credentials. Buyers use their own accounts and tokens.
Golf booking sites are typically used in the browser (Chronogolf, MemberSports, EZLinks-style portals, and similar). Each course may have its own login and release window.

name: tee-time-setup

  Use when installing or reconfiguring Tee Timey: courses, preferred windows,
  party size, and drop schedules.
---
# Tee Time setup

Use when a buyer first installs Tee Timey, or when they want to change courses, windows, party size, or drop schedules.

## Goal
Get a working DIY tee-time sniper on the buyer's own Grok Bot account using their courses, logins, and preferred times. No seller support is included.

## Collect from the buyer
1. Ordered course priority (highest first) and which booking site each uses (Chronogolf, MemberSports, EZLinks-style, other).
2. Preferred morning tee window (start–end inclusive). Default suggestion if they are unsure: 8:00am–10:00am.
3. Party size preference (default: prefer 2, fall back to 1 if 2 is unavailable).
4. Target play day (often Saturday) and how many days ahead each site releases.
5. Release clock times in their local timezone for each booking system.

## Configure
1. Write profile memories for party size, window, priority list, and upgrade rules (generalized — never store passwords).
2. Update drop routines' schedules to the buyer's timezone and release times (early primary + on-the-hour safety net; add a separate late-window pair if a course uses a different release clock).
3. Retarget routine job text to their course names and sites; keep login/captcha handoff and never-after-window rules.
4. Have the buyer sign into each golf site on this computer once (handoff); do not invent credentials.

## Smoke test
Run a dry check of availability for the next target date without booking unless the buyer asks. Confirm notifications work on a routine wake.

## Out of scope
Do not sell, market, or collect payment. Do not use anyone else's golf logins. Buyers are responsible for each golf site's terms.

routines.name: Primary tee time drop
routines.description: Fires early before the main online tee-time window so the bot can prep and grab the earliest preferred slot.
routines.content:
PRIMARY evening tee-time drop. Fire early on purpose (about 20 minutes before the buyer's main online window) so prep finishes before release.

On wake: notify the buyer that the drop is awake and prepping. Then work.

Hard rules:
- Target play date = the buyer's configured target (often Saturday exactly N days out matching their main booking window)
- 18 holes (not par-3 / not Back 9 unless the buyer says otherwise)
- Tee time only inside the buyer's preferred morning window — never after it ends
- Within that window, always book the EARLIEST available qualifying time
- Party size: prefer 2 players; if no 2-player slot in the window, book 1 player
- Login/captcha: hand the buyer the computer; never invent credentials

Course priority: ordered list from buyer memory (highest first).

Upgrade ranking (best to worst):
1) 2-player at a higher-priority course
2) 2-player earlier time
3) 1-player at a higher-priority course
4) 1-player earlier time
A 2-player hold beats a 1-player hold unless the buyer says otherwise. On a higher-priority success, cancel the lower hold (notify before cancel when a fee may apply). Never leave duplicates for the same play date.

Flow:
1. Warm the primary booking site session before the window opens; at open, try courses in priority order ASAP.
2. If the primary site fails, try any secondary booking systems the buyer configured.
3. Courses with a different release schedule may use a separate routine — skip them here if out of window.
4. Never book outside the preferred window. Notify every outcome.

A separate safety-net routine may fire at window open — if you already booked a qualifying hold, it should no-op unless a clear upgrade is available.

Keep durable unless paused/deleted.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Denver 40 18 * * 6`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Primary tee time safety net
routines.description: Fires at the main tee-time release time as a backup if the early primary drop missed.
routines.content:
SAFETY NET for the primary tee-time drop. Fire at the buyer's main online window open time.

Purpose: if the primary drop did not wake or did not finish a qualifying booking, do the grab now. Do NOT duplicate work.

Hard rules if booking: 18 holes, preferred morning window ONLY, earliest time in that window, never after it ends. Prefer 2 players; if no 2-player slot, book 1. Course order from buyer memory. Upgrade ranking: 2-player higher-priority beats 2-player lower; any 2-player beats any 1-player; then earlier time. Cancel/upgrade lower placeholders. Login/captcha handoff.

On wake:
1. Notify the buyer briefly that the safety net fired.
2. Check reservations for the target play date. If a qualifying booking already exists, notify “already covered” and stop unless a clear upgrade appeared.
3. If nothing qualifying is booked, run the full cascade ASAP (2 then 1).
4. Notify success or exact failure. Never outside the preferred window.

Keep durable unless paused/deleted.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Denver 0 19 * * 6`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
